questions.question: What scale of work and spend does the technology review expect to bring the unsupported framework code up to date?

questions.question: If the company changes hands, what can its biggest customer do under the contract, and how much notice applies?
questions.expected_answer: The largest customer can terminate after a change of ownership by giving 90 days' notice.

questions.question: Once the one-off telematics sale is stripped out, do the retention figures from management and the cohort work agree?
questions.expected_answer: No. Management reports 112% NRR on its year-end ARR basis; cohort analysis gives 104% excluding the one-off bundle and 111% including it on recognised revenue. The difference reflects the measurement basis.

questions.question: Can we keep the 80% recurring-revenue label after the QoE treatment of implementation and training fees?
questions.expected_answer: The figures differ by definition: management reports 80%, including the fees, while the draft QoE treats EUR 8m of implementation and training fees as non-recurring and calculates 71%.
questions.author: Independent human reviewer (source-document based; implementation not inspected)

questions.question: Why did the seller's FY2025 sales number fall in the restated information memorandum, and what figure replaced it?
questions.expected_answer: The second CIM removes hardware pass-through (telematics devices resold at cost) and restates FY2025 revenue from EUR 92m to EUR 88m.

questions.question: Track the adjusted EBITDA stated in the first CIM and the restated CIM. What changed?
